transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m here because at night, once I start eating, I can’t seem to stop. I’m telling myself to quit, but I just keep reaching for more anyway.
When this happens, do you eat what most people would consider a very large amount of food?
Yes. I might start with leftovers, then have sandwiches, cereal, cookies—whatever snack food is around. By the end, it’s a lot more than I’d ever eat for a normal supper.
After these episodes, do you make yourself vomit?
I’m not sure what you mean by “make myself.” I feel pretty bad afterward, but I haven’t really thought about it that way.
After you overeat, do you ever make yourself throw up?
I… I don’t know. I feel awful after eating like that, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m making myself throw up.
After you eat this way, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I’m honestly not sure. I feel sick and ashamed afterward, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m doing that on purpose.
After these eating episodes, do you ever use laxatives to try to get rid of the food?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to doing anything like that after I eat.
After these eating episodes, do you ever fast for a whole day or skip meals the next day to make up for the eating?

Yeah. After a bad night of eating, I’ll skip breakfast and lunch the next day to try to make up for it. Sometimes I’ll walk way farther than I normally would too, even when my knees are telling me to head home.
Do you ever try to undo these eating episodes by making yourself throw up?
I don’t know. I feel pretty upset afterward, but I haven’t really noticed whether I’m making myself throw up.
How often do you skip meals the next day after these nighttime eating episodes?
For the last several months, it’s been at least once most weeks. I’ll have a night like that, then the next day I try to make up for it by skipping meals or being really strict about food.
How much does your body shape or weight affect how you feel about yourself?

A lot lately. I used to feel good about myself based on my work—solving a design problem, helping out at the theater. But now I look at my stomach in the mirror and it feels like that’s the whole measure of me: whether I look controlled or sloppy.
How often do these overeating episodes happen?
For the last several months, it’s been at least one night most weeks. Then I usually spend the next day trying to make up for it—skipping meals, making strict rules, or taking an extra-long walk.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not sure what counts as significantly low. I haven’t really thought of myself that way.
What is your current height and weight?
I don’t know my exact current weight. I’m about average height, I think, but I haven’t measured either recently.
Have other people told you that you are underweight?
No, not that I can remember. Nobody’s really said anything to me about being underweight.
During these eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yes. Once I start eating at night, I keep telling myself to stop, but I just keep reaching for more. It feels like I’m watching myself do it and can’t really make myself quit.
Besides skipping meals and taking extra-long walks, do you ever use any other method to try to get rid of the food after these eating episodes?
I’m not sure what else you mean. I’ve mostly just skipped meals or gone walking afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you ever take diet pills or water pills to try to undo the eating?
No, I haven’t taken anything like that.
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever try to undo the eating by taking laxatives?
No, I haven’t used laxatives.
For the past 3 months, have these nighttime overeating episodes happened at least once a week?

Yes. For the last several months, it’s been at least once most weeks. Then I usually spend the next day trying to make up for it—skipping meals, making strict rules about food, or taking a really long walk.
Has your weight been low enough that a doctor or someone close to you has been concerned you were underweight?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought of myself as underweight.
